records.title: Germination
records.summary: Germination: From sowing until seedlings are up, usually the first week or two.
instructions: Check sown spots every day or two.
Break any crust over sown spots gently with a fingertip.
Note in the journal how many spots came up.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Germination
records.timing_description: From sowing until seedlings are up, usually the first week or two.
records.water: Soil must stay moist. If a dry gap follows sowing, give a cupful of stored water per spot every couple of days.
records.mulch: Do not cover the sown spot with mulch until seedlings show; mulch the surrounding soil instead.
records.nutrients: Rely on the compost or organic matter already mixed into pits and beds; add nothing on top of seeds.
records.weeds: Pull weeds by hand around sowing spots so they do not compete.
watch_for: Ants, termites or birds taking seed
records.dry_spell: If the soil dries out before seedlings appear, water sparingly from storage; if many spots fail, re-sow with reserved seed once rains return.
actions: Check sown spots every day or two.
Break any crust over sown spots gently with a fingertip.
Note in the journal how many spots came up.

records.title: Seedling
records.summary: Seedling: From emergence to a few weeks old, with several leaves.
instructions: Thin to the strongest plants per spot.
Mulch.
Weed by hand.
Check for pests every few days.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Seedling
records.timing_description: From emergence to a few weeks old, with several leaves.
records.water: Water only in dry spells, a cupful at the base in the morning or evening.
records.mulch: Spread mulch around seedlings, a finger's width away from the stems, about a hand's depth.
records.nutrients: If seedlings look pale, work a handful of compost or rotted manure into the soil around (not touching) them.
records.weeds: Weed by hand regularly; weeds steal scarce water and nutrients.
records.dry_spell: In a dry spell, thicken the mulch, shade with a few leafy twigs, and give stored water to the weakest pits first.
actions: Thin to the strongest plants per spot.
Mulch.
Weed by hand.
Check for pests every few days.

records.title: Leafy growth
records.summary: Leafy growth: From a few weeks after sowing until flowering begins.
instructions: Weed and mulch.
Top up compost if plants look hungry.
Watch for pests and striga.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Leafy growth
records.timing_description: From a few weeks after sowing until flowering begins.
records.water: Rain should carry the crop; use stored water only if plants wilt and do not recover by morning.
records.mulch: Keep the mulch topped up as termites and weather break it down.
records.nutrients: A top-up of compost or rotted manure around plants can help if they look pale; no fixed recipe applies.
records.weeds: Weed once or twice more; lay pulled weeds (without seeds) as mulch.
records.dry_spell: The mid-season dry spell often comes now: thicken mulch, stop all weeding that disturbs soil, and save water for flowering.
actions: Weed and mulch.
Top up compost if plants look hungry.
Watch for pests and striga.

records.title: Flowering
records.summary: Flowering: When flowers or heads appear, until grain or pods start filling.
instructions: Watch for pests daily.
Protect heads from birds.
Use stored water if plants wilt.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Flowering
records.timing_description: When flowers or heads appear, until grain or pods start filling.
records.water: This is the most water-sensitive stage: if a dry spell hits now, use stored water on the best plants first.
records.mulch: Keep the soil fully covered.
records.nutrients: Do not add fresh manure now; the plant is using what is in the soil.
records.weeds: Light hand-weeding only; avoid disturbing roots.
records.dry_spell: Prioritise stored water for flowering plants; shade is less important than moisture now.
actions: Watch for pests daily.
Protect heads from birds.
Use stored water if plants wilt.

records.title: Ripening
records.summary: Ripening: From grain or pod filling until harvest.
instructions: Guard against birds.
Prepare a clean, dry place and containers for drying and storage.
Choose the best plants for seed saving.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Ripening
records.timing_description: From grain or pod filling until harvest.
records.water: Stop watering as grain or pods dry; dry weather now helps.
records.mulch: Leave mulch in place; it will be the next season's organic matter.
records.nutrients: No feeding needed.
records.weeds: Pull any weeds before they set seed.
watch_for: Mould on heads or pods in wet weather
records.dry_spell: A dry spell now usually does little harm; harvest promptly if plants are drying fast.
actions: Guard against birds.
Prepare a clean, dry place and containers for drying and storage.
Choose the best plants for seed saving.

records.title: Millet leafy growth and tillering
records.summary: Millet leafy growth and tillering: From about three weeks after sowing until heads begin to show.
instructions: Pull striga before it flowers.
Weed and mulch.
Note which pits grow best.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Millet leafy growth and tillering
records.timing_description: From about three weeks after sowing until heads begin to show.
records.water: Millets tolerate short dry spells; water only if plants roll their leaves all day and stay rolled by morning.
records.mulch: Keep mulch between plants; it reduces crusting after hard rain.
records.nutrients: If leaves are pale, add a handful of compost or rotted manure around each pit; a legume neighbour also helps.
records.weeds: Weed by hand early; millets are slow to cover the ground.
watch_for: Striga (witchweed) with pink or purple flowers near millet
records.dry_spell: Thicken mulch; millets usually recover when rain returns.
actions: Pull striga before it flowers.
Weed and mulch.
Note which pits grow best.

records.title: Millet heading and flowering
records.summary: Millet heading and flowering: When heads emerge until grains begin to fill.
instructions: Start bird scaring as grains fill.
Pull striga before it seeds and remove it from the field.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Millet heading and flowering
records.timing_description: When heads emerge until grains begin to fill.
records.water: Moisture now matters most; save stored water for this stage.
records.mulch: Keep soil covered.
records.nutrients: No feeding needed now.
records.weeds: Pull striga and weeds before they set seed.
watch_for: Leaf and head spots (blast) in humid weather
records.dry_spell: If a dry spell hits now, give stored water to the best pits; heads that do not fill will not recover later.
actions: Start bird scaring as grains fill.
Pull striga before it seeds and remove it from the field.

records.title: Legume leafy growth
records.summary: Legume leafy growth: From a few weeks after sowing until flowering.
instructions: Check undersides of leaves for aphids.
Open an overflow notch if water stands in pits.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Legume leafy growth
records.timing_description: From a few weeks after sowing until flowering.
records.water: Legumes dislike waterlogging more than dryness: make sure water drains from pits and beds after heavy rain.
records.mulch: Mulch around plants; keep it off stems.
records.nutrients: Legumes make much of their own nitrogen; compost already in the pit is usually enough.
records.weeds: Weed by hand early, before the vines spread.
records.dry_spell: Thicken mulch; pick only a few leaves for food during dry spells.
actions: Check undersides of leaves for aphids.
Open an overflow notch if water stands in pits.

records.title: Legume flowering and pod set
records.summary: Legume flowering and pod set: When flowers appear until pods are filling.
instructions: Check flowers and pods every few days; hand-pick caterpillars.
Use neem extract only if pests are building up.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Legume flowering and pod set
records.timing_description: When flowers appear until pods are filling.
records.water: Flowers drop if the plant is very dry; use stored water now if a dry spell comes.
records.mulch: Keep soil covered.
records.nutrients: No feeding needed.
records.weeds: Light hand-weeding only.
watch_for: Pod borers (holes in pods, caterpillars inside flowers)
records.dry_spell: Water the best plants first; a short dry spell can cost many flowers.
actions: Check flowers and pods every few days; hand-pick caterpillars.
Use neem extract only if pests are building up.

records.title: Groundnut flowering and pegging
records.summary: Groundnut flowering and pegging: When flowers appear and pegs push into the soil.
instructions: Gently loosen crusted soil around plants before pegging begins.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Groundnut flowering and pegging
records.timing_description: When flowers appear and pegs push into the soil.
records.water: Pegs need moist, loose soil; water from storage if the bed surface is dry and hard.
records.mulch: Keep mulch light near the plant so pegs can reach the soil; mulch the bed edges thickly.
records.nutrients: No feeding needed.
records.weeds: Do not disturb the soil around plants once pegging starts.
watch_for: Pegs failing to enter hard soil
records.dry_spell: Keep the bed surface moist and loose; pegging fails in dry crusted soil.
actions: Gently loosen crusted soil around plants before pegging begins.

records.title: Tree planting-out
records.summary: Tree planting-out: From planting the seedling or cutting until it shows new leaves, the first weeks.
instructions: Firm soil around the seedling after heavy rain.
Fence with thorny branches against animals.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Tree planting-out
records.timing_description: From planting the seedling or cutting until it shows new leaves, the first weeks.
records.water: Keep the root zone moist: a cupful or two from storage every few days if rain stops.
records.mulch: Mulch widely around the tree, a hand's width clear of the stem.
records.nutrients: Compost is already in the enlarged pit; add nothing fresh against the roots.
records.weeds: Keep a circle around the tree free of weeds.
watch_for: Wilting that does not recover by morning
records.dry_spell: Shade with a few leafy branches and give stored water every few days.
actions: Firm soil around the seedling after heavy rain.
Fence with thorny branches against animals.

records.title: Young tree, first wet season
records.summary: Young tree, first wet season: From new leaves until the end of the first wet season.
instructions: Repair the basin or half-moon after storms.
Keep thorny protection in place.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Young tree, first wet season
records.timing_description: From new leaves until the end of the first wet season.
records.water: Rain should be enough; water only in long dry spells.
records.mulch: Top up mulch before the rains end.
records.nutrients: A bucketful of compost or rotted manure worked lightly around the basin edge can help.
records.weeds: Keep the circle around the tree weed-free.
records.dry_spell: Shade and water from storage during long dry spells.
actions: Repair the basin or half-moon after storms.
Keep thorny protection in place.

records.title: Tree through its first dry seasons
records.summary: Tree through its first dry seasons: The first one or two dry seasons after planting.
instructions: Clear a firebreak around young trees.
Extend the basin as the tree grows.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
safety_notes: Never burn grass near young trees.
records.label: Tree through its first dry seasons
records.timing_description: The first one or two dry seasons after planting.
records.water: Give stored water now and then through the first dry season, more for mango than for cashew or gliricidia.
records.mulch: A thick mulch ring is the most important protection in the dry season.
records.nutrients: Add compost or leaf litter to the mulch ring before each wet season.
records.weeds: Cut (do not dig) weeds in the ring.
watch_for: Leaf drop and dieback in the dry season
Fire risk from dry grass nearby
records.dry_spell: Mulch, shade and occasional stored water; clear dry grass from around young trees as a firebreak.
actions: Clear a firebreak around young trees.
Extend the basin as the tree grows.

records.title: Tree flowering and fruit set
records.summary: Tree flowering and fruit set: Once trees are old enough to flower, usually in the dry season.
instructions: Clear the ground beneath the tree before nut fall.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Tree flowering and fruit set
records.timing_description: Once trees are old enough to flower, usually in the dry season.
records.water: Mature trees need no watering; avoid watering during flowering unless trees are very stressed.
records.mulch: Keep leaf litter under the canopy.
records.nutrients: Add compost to the basin before the rains, not during flowering.
records.weeds: Keep the area under the canopy clear for collecting fallen nuts or fruit.
watch_for: Shoot and flower damage by sucking bugs (such as tea mosquito bug on cashew)
records.dry_spell: Mature trees cope; young trees in their first flowering may be helped with stored water.
actions: Clear the ground beneath the tree before nut fall.

records.title: Tree fruit ripening
records.summary: Tree fruit ripening: From fruit set until nuts or fruit are ready.
instructions: Collect fallen nuts often (daily in wet weather).
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Tree fruit ripening
records.timing_description: From fruit set until nuts or fruit are ready.
records.water: No watering needed for mature trees.
records.mulch: Keep the ground under trees clean for collection.
records.nutrients: None now.
records.weeds: Keep clear under the canopy.
records.dry_spell: No action needed for mature trees.
actions: Collect fallen nuts often (daily in wet weather).

records.title: Gliricidia lopping for mulch
records.summary: Gliricidia lopping for mulch: Once the hedge is well established, usually within about a year.
instructions: Lop leafy branches above knee height a few times per season.
Lay leaves on beds as green manure.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Gliricidia lopping for mulch
records.timing_description: Once the hedge is well established, usually within about a year.
records.water: No watering once established.
records.mulch: Its leaves are the mulch: lay them on beds and pits.
records.nutrients: Leaves feed the soil as they rot.
records.weeds: Keep the hedge line clear of climbing weeds.
records.dry_spell: Lop less in long dry spells so the hedge recovers.
actions: Lop leafy branches above knee height a few times per season.
Lay leaves on beds as green manure.

records.title: Cuttings and slips taking root
records.summary: Cuttings and slips taking root: From planting cuttings, tops or slips until new leaves show, usually the first couple of weeks.
instructions: Firm soil around cuttings after heavy rain.
Replace failed cuttings promptly.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Cuttings and slips taking root
records.timing_description: From planting cuttings, tops or slips until new leaves show, usually the first couple of weeks.
records.water: Keep the soil around cuttings damp: a cupful of stored water every couple of days if rain stops.
records.mulch: Mulch around, not over, the cuttings.
records.nutrients: Compost already in the mound or bed is enough; add nothing fresh.
records.weeds: Keep weeds away from the young cuttings.
records.dry_spell: Shade with a few leafy twigs and water from storage; replace dead cuttings while the soil is still moist.
actions: Firm soil around cuttings after heavy rain.
Replace failed cuttings promptly.

records.title: Root crops: vine and leaf growth
records.summary: Root crops: vine and leaf growth: From rooting until roots begin to swell, roughly the middle of the season.
instructions: Pile soil over cracks in sweet potato mounds.
Pull and remove cassava plants with mosaic signs.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Root crops: vine and leaf growth
records.timing_description: From rooting until roots begin to swell, roughly the middle of the season.
records.water: Rain is usually enough once rooted; water only if leaves wilt and stay wilted.
records.mulch: Keep mulch between mounds; vines of sweet potato soon cover the ground themselves.
records.nutrients: Use only moderate compost: very rich soil gives leaves instead of roots.
records.weeds: Weed until vines or leaves cover the ground.
records.dry_spell: Thicken mulch; established root crops ride out dry spells well.
actions: Pile soil over cracks in sweet potato mounds.
Pull and remove cassava plants with mosaic signs.

records.title: Pineapple growth
records.summary: Pineapple growth: The long growing period before flowering, often more than a year.
instructions: Remove side shoots (slips) for new plants once they are a hand long.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Pineapple growth
records.timing_description: The long growing period before flowering, often more than a year.
records.water: Rain only once rooted; it stores water in its leaves.
records.mulch: Keep a mulch ring; do not let mulch pile against the base.
records.nutrients: A handful of compost around the plant at the start of each wet season.
records.weeds: Keep the base weed-free.
watch_for: Rot at the base in standing water
records.dry_spell: No special action; mulch.
actions: Remove side shoots (slips) for new plants once they are a hand long.

records.title: Pineapple fruiting
records.summary: Pineapple fruiting: From the appearance of the fruit until it ripens.
instructions: Protect ripening fruit with thorny branches or a cloth cover.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Pineapple fruiting
records.timing_description: From the appearance of the fruit until it ripens.
records.water: Rain only.
records.mulch: Keep mulch in place.
records.nutrients: None needed.
records.weeds: Keep the base weed-free.
watch_for: Animals and birds at ripening fruit
records.dry_spell: No special action.
actions: Protect ripening fruit with thorny branches or a cloth cover.

records.title: Greens picking period
records.summary: Greens picking period: From about four weeks after sowing for as long as leaves keep coming.
instructions: Pick young leaves every few days.
Pinch out flower heads unless saving seed.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Greens picking period
records.timing_description: From about four weeks after sowing for as long as leaves keep coming.
records.water: Keep the soil damp under mulch; water at the base in the cool of the day in dry spells.
records.mulch: Keep mulch topped up around plants.
records.nutrients: A handful of compost worked around plants every few weeks keeps leaves coming.
records.weeds: Pull weeds by hand.
watch_for: Caterpillars and aphids on young leaves
Plants rushing to flower in heat or dryness
records.dry_spell: Shade at midday with a few twigs and give stored water at the base.
actions: Pick young leaves every few days.
Pinch out flower heads unless saving seed.

records.title: Green manure ready to cut
records.summary: Green manure ready to cut: As the first flowers open, roughly six to nine weeks after sowing.
instructions: Cut as flowers open and lay on beds or mix into pits.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Green manure ready to cut
records.timing_description: As the first flowers open, roughly six to nine weeks after sowing.
records.water: Rain only.
records.mulch: The cut crop becomes the mulch.
records.nutrients: The cut crop itself feeds the soil.
records.weeds: None needed under a thick stand.
watch_for: Stems turning woody if left too long
records.dry_spell: No action.
actions: Cut as flowers open and lay on beds or mix into pits.

records.title: Grass hedge upkeep
records.summary: Grass hedge upkeep: Through each season once the slips have rooted.
instructions: Fill gaps with new slips.
Trim to about knee-high and use the cuttings as mulch.
limitations: Timings are approximate; follow how the plants look.
records.label: Grass hedge upkeep
records.timing_description: Through each season once the slips have rooted.
records.water: Rain only once rooted.
records.mulch: Trimmings are mulch for nearby beds.
records.nutrients: None needed.
records.weeds: Keep spreading weeds out of the hedge line.
watch_for: Gaps in the hedge where water cuts through
records.dry_spell: No action; established hedges cope.
actions: Fill gaps with new slips.
Trim to about knee-high and use the cuttings as mulch.
